It uses the local helper `has_error_or_infer` to suppress noisy diagnostics for error or inference types.
Local helper that returns whether any type in an iterator is already erroneous or still an inference variable, allowing diagnostics to avoid low-value output.

Determines the type of a literal expression, using literal suffixes when present and otherwise biasing unsuffixed integer/float literals from the expected type before falling back to fresh inference variables. It directly calls `self.next_int_var` and `self.next_float_var` when no suitable expected type is available.

Resolves a path used in struct/variant/union construction, verifies that the resolved type is an appropriate ADT variant, records user type annotations, adds obligations for its substitutions, and emits E0071 when the path does not name a struct-like type. It directly calls `self.finish_resolving_struct_path`, `self.set_tainted_by_errors`, `self.write_user_type_annotation_from_substs`, and `self.add_required_obligations`.

Type-checks a local initializer against the declared local type, avoiding coercions when the pattern contains explicit `ref` bindings and otherwise permitting normal coercion. It directly calls `self.local_ty`, `self.check_expr_with_needs`, `self.demand_eqtype`, and `self.check_expr_coercable_to_type`.

Type-checks a local declaration by writing its declared type, checking the initializer, overriding local types on error to reduce cascades, checking the pattern against the declaration type, and validating `let ... else` blocks as diverging. It directly calls `self.local_ty`, `self.write_ty`, `self.check_decl_initializer`, `self.overwrite_local_ty_if_err`, `self.check_pat_top`, `self.node_ty`, `self.check_block_with_expected`, `self.cause`, and `self.demand_eqtype_with_origin`.
Thin wrapper that converts an HIR local into a generic declaration form and forwards it for checking. It directly calls `self.check_decl`.

Type-checks a statement while preserving and restoring divergence/error state, skipping item statements, checking local declarations, requiring bare expression statements to have unit type, and using a special expectation for final `match` semicolon statements to improve diagnostics. It directly calls `self.warn_if_unreachable`, `self.check_decl_local`, `self.check_expr_has_type_or_error`, `self.suggest_semicolon_at_end`, and `self.check_expr_with_expectation`.
Type-checks a block in a unit context and then enforces that any non-diverging block result is a subtype of `()`. It directly calls `self.check_block_with_expected` and `self.demand_suptype`.

Type-checks a block under an expected type by creating the appropriate breakable coercion context, checking each statement, checking the tail expression with the provided expectation, coercing tail/break values into a merged block type, and emitting targeted diagnostics for forced-unit or mismatched tail expressions. It directly calls `self.check_stmt`, `self.check_expr_with_expectation`, `self.get_expr_coercion_span`, `self.cause`, `self.suggest_block_to_brackets`, `self.get_parent_fn_decl`, `self.parent_item_span`, `self.misc`, `self.only_has_type`, `self.consider_removing_semicolon`, and `self.consider_returning_binding`.
Finds the span of the enclosing function or impl method body block for a given HIR node, returning `None` when the parent item is not a function-like block.
Looks up the parent item of a block and extracts its function declaration and identifier when the parent is function-like. It directly calls `self.get_node_fn_decl`.

Chooses a more precise span for expression coercion diagnostics by preferring the active tail of `if`/`match`/block expressions when type checking has already established a non-`!` type, and otherwise falling back to the expression span.

When a local or pattern type resolves to an error type, overwrites the recorded types for both HIR nodes and updates the locals table so later checks do not cascade from stale types. It directly calls `self.write_ty`.

Completes type resolution for a struct-like path across resolved, type-relative, and lang-item forms, producing both the resolution and the resulting type while updating stored resolution info for type-relative paths. It directly calls `self.to_ty`, `AstConv::res_to_ty`, `AstConv::associated_path_to_ty`, `self.write_resolution`, and `self.resolve_lang_item_path`.

Refines fulfillment-error spans so diagnostics point at the specific call argument responsible for a trait obligation failure instead of the whole call, while avoiding desugared spans and tracing derived obligations back to their top-level cause. It uses the local helper `unpeel_to_top` to recover the originating obligation cause.
Local helper that walks through nested derived-obligation cause codes and returns the highest-level originating cause code.

Refines fulfillment-error spans for function calls with explicit generic arguments by moving the blame from the full call to the particular type argument whose resolved type matches the failing trait predicate. It directly calls `self.resolve_vars_if_possible`.

Checks whether removing a trailing semicolon from the block could satisfy the expected type, and if so emits either a boxing-aware verbose suggestion or a simple semicolon-removal suggestion. This method calls `could_remove_semicolon` and then uses `span_suggestion_verbose` or `span_suggestion_short` to report the fix.

Annotates an error with the definition site of a function-like item or closure. For local function-like items, it collects the identifier span and parameter spans and emits a note describing where the item was defined; for closures without an identifier span, it falls back to the closure declaration span. This method calls query/accessor helpers such as `def_ident_span`, `hir`, `get_if_local`, `body_id`, `body`, `def_kind`, and emits diagnostics via `push_span_label` and `span_note`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/check/callee.r: Rejects illegal explicit `Drop::drop` method calls by checking whether the trait is the lang-item `drop_trait`, then emits a diagnostic with a `drop(...)` suggestion built from the receiver snippet when available. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Main entry point for type-checking `callee(args)`: it type-checks the callee expression, runs autoderef, repeatedly calls `try_overloaded_call_step` to classify the call as builtin, deferred-closure, or overloaded, then dispatches to `confirm_builtin_call`, `confirm_deferred_closure_call`, or `confirm_overloaded_call` accordingly, and finally registers a well-formedness obligation on the result.

Examines one autoderef step of the callee to decide how the call should proceed: it recognizes direct builtin calls for `FnDef`/`FnPtr`, defers unresolved closure calls by recording enough information for later, and otherwise tries overloaded `Fn*` trait dispatch. This method calls `try_overloaded_call_traits` to probe trait-based call resolution.

Attempts overloaded call resolution by probing the `Fn`, `FnMut`, and `FnOnce` lang traits in order, performing trait-method lookup for the synthesized tuple of argument types and computing any required autoref adjustment for the receiver. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Detects the parser pattern where a closure body is immediately followed by call syntax without parentheses, including async-closure wrapping cases, and adds a multipart suggestion to wrap the closure in parentheses. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Recognizes mistaken array syntax where tuple-like call syntax appears inside an array literal and suggests inserting a comma between elements. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Validates a direct builtin function or function-pointer call by extracting the function signature, optionally evaluating annotated where-clauses for diagnostics, and otherwise producing detailed errors and syntax suggestions when the callee is not callable. For diagnostics, this method calls `identify_bad_closure_def_and_call` and `maybe_suggest_bad_array_definition` from the Methods List.

Checks argument types for a closure call whose closure kind has not yet been fixed, using the known closure signature to derive expected input types and returning the closure’s output type. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Finalizes an overloaded trait-based call by type-checking method-call arguments with tuple-argument handling, recording the resolved `MethodCallee`, and returning the method’s output type. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Completes a previously deferred closure call once closure-kind inference is known: it calls `try_overloaded_call_traits` to resolve the appropriate `Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce` method, equates the newly chosen method signature with the earlier closure signature, applies stored adjustments plus any autoref, and records the resolved method call; otherwise it emits an error if no call trait lang item exists.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/mod.r: Builds or reuses the MIR body for a local item. If `def.try_upgrade(tcx)` succeeds, it delegates to `tcx.mir_built`; otherwise it calls `mir_build` to construct MIR, adjusts the source for const-parameter instances with `MirSource::from_instance`, and returns the allocated stolen MIR via `tcx.alloc_steal_mir`.

Main MIR-construction dispatcher for a body owner. It queries HIR/typeck state, forces prerequisite unsafety and abstract-const analyses, identifies the body/return-type span from HIR, then builds an inference context and dispatches to either `construct_fn`, `construct_const`, or `construct_error` depending on the item kind and whether THIR/typeck construction failed.

Computes the closure environment type with late-bound regions liberated for MIR building. It reads the closure type from `tcx.typeck_body(body_id).node_type`, derives the environment type with `tcx.closure_env_ty`, and erases the late-bound region binder with `tcx.erase_late_bound_regions`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a tail-expression context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::TailExpr`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a statement context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::Statement`.
Checks whether a local variable id is currently tracked in any active match-guard frame by scanning `guard_context` with nested iterator `any` tests.
Maps a THIR local-variable id to the MIR local to use in the current guard mode. It calls `LocalsForNode::local_id` on the entry stored in `self.var_indices`.
Creates an empty `BlockContext` with no active block frames.
Pushes a `BlockFrame` onto the block-context stack.
Pops and returns the most recent `BlockFrame` from the block-context stack.
Finds the nearest enclosing tail-expression frame that is not masked by a statement frame by iterating the block-context stack in reverse, and returns its tail-result metadata if present.
Reports whether the current block context should ignore a tail expression's result, based on the last active frame in the stack.
Constructs a `GuardFrameLocal` that records only the bound local variable id for guard tracking.

Selects the MIR local to use for a binding, choosing between the ordinary local and the guard-specific reference local depending on `ForGuard`, and bugs if a single-local binding is incorrectly requested from within a guard.
Trait method that combines a basic block with an arbitrary value into a `BlockAnd<T>` pair.
Trait method that converts a basic block into a `BlockAnd<()>` pair carrying unit.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` and a supplied value into `BlockAnd<T>`.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` into `BlockAnd<()>` with a unit payload.

Builds MIR for a function or closure body. It collects arguments, creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, enters call-site and argument scopes via `builder.in_scope`, enters the return breakable scope with `builder.in_breakable_scope`, lowers parameters and the body by calling `builder.args_and_body`, emits the final return terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, finalizes drops with `builder.build_drop_trees`, uses `return_block.unit()` to package the scope result, and completes the MIR with `builder.finish`.

Builds MIR for a constant or static initializer. It creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, lowers the THIR expression into the return place by calling `builder.expr_into_dest`, emits a `Return` terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, runs `builder.build_drop_trees`, and returns the finished body from `builder.finish`.

Constructs fallback error MIR for items whose earlier compilation stages failed. It computes parameter count from HIR, creates minimal CFG/source-scope/local-decl state, adds parameter locals, terminates the start block as `Unreachable` with `cfg.terminate`, builds the body with `Body::new`, and records a generator yield type when applicable.

Initializes the MIR `Builder` state for a body, computing overflow-check behavior, parameter/typeck/region context, CFG and local tables, and other bookkeeping. It also initializes the CFG start block with `builder.cfg.start_new_block` and creates the outermost source scope by calling `builder.new_source_scope`.
Finalizes MIR construction. It validates that every basic block has a terminator by iterating the CFG, then creates the finished MIR body with `Body::new`.

Allocates MIR locals for function arguments, records argument debug info, prepares closure/generator capture metadata and upvar debug info when needed, schedules capture drops, and lowers argument patterns and the function body into MIR. During argument lowering it calls `self.set_correct_source_scope_for_arg` to adjust lint/source scopes for each argument pattern.

Adjusts the current source scope when an argument pattern belongs to a different lint-level root than its parent scope. If the roots differ, it creates a replacement scope by calling `self.new_source_scope`.
Returns a cached temporary place for unit values, creating it on first use by calling `self.temp` with `tcx.mk_unit()` and then storing the result in `self.unit_temp`.
Parses a float literal into a `ConstValue` by calling `parse_float_into_scalar` and mapping the resulting scalar to `ConstValue::Scalar`.

Parses a float literal symbol into a MIR `Scalar` for either `f32` or `f64`. It parses both Rust and apfloat representations, asserts that their bit patterns agree, applies negation when requested, and returns the value via `Scalar::from_f32` or `Scalar::from_f64`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/instance.rs: Returns the instantiated callable type for this instance by calling `self.def.def_id()` to identify the definition, `tcx.type_of(...)` to fetch its declared type, and `tcx.instantiate_and_normalize_erasing_regions(...)` to apply `self.args` and normalize it in the given typing environment.

Checks whether this instance can reuse an upstream shared monomorphization. It early-exits based on `share_generics`, `self.def_id().is_local()`, `self.args.non_erasable_generics().next()`, and `is_compiler_builtins`, then for `InstanceKind::Item` calls `tcx.upstream_monomorphizations_for(def)` and looks up `self.args`, for `DropGlue` calls `tcx.upstream_drop_glue_for(self.args)`, and for `AsyncDropGlueCtorShim` calls `tcx.upstream_async_drop_glue_for(self.args)`.
Returns the originating `DefId` for any `InstanceDef` variant by pattern-matching and extracting the stored definition id. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.

Returns `Some(def_id)` only for instances whose code may be available from elsewhere instead of always requiring guaranteed local codegen, specifically plain items, typed drop glue, and thread-local shims; returns `None` for shim-only or always-local-generated variants. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.
Fetches attributes with the requested name for this instance from `TyCtxt`. This method calls `InstanceDef::def_id` to obtain the underlying definition id before querying attributes.

Determines whether this instance must be treated as inline: most shim-like variants return `true`, typed drop glue and thread-local shims return `false`, and plain items are inlined only when their definition path is a constructor or closure expression. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.

Decides whether codegen should emit a CGU-internal copy of this instance. It first calls `InstanceDef::requires_inline`; for typed drop glue it applies extra incremental-compilation and ADT/destructor heuristics, for thread-local shims it returns `false`, and otherwise it uses the instance's codegen inline attributes. This method also calls `InstanceDef::def_id` for the final attribute lookup.

Checks whether calling this instance requires an implicit caller-location argument: item and virtual instances consult `#[track_caller]` codegen flags, closure-once shims use their stored `track_caller` flag, and all other variants return `false`. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.

Reports whether the instance kind has a polymorphic MIR body that can be instantiated generically. Clone shims, thread-local shims, fn-pointer address/pointer shims, and typed drop glue return `false`, while ordinary items, most shims, virtual calls, intrinsics, and untyped drop glue return `true`. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.
Formats a full instance display by calling `fmt_instance(f, *self, None)`.
Constructs a plain item instance after asserting that `args.has_escaping_bound_vars()` is false, storing the result as `InstanceKind::Item(def_id)` with the provided arguments.
Builds a monomorphic instance for a non-generic definition by calling `GenericArgs::for_item(...)` to synthesize erased lifetime arguments and then calling `Instance::new(def_id, args)`.
Returns this instance's definition id by calling `self.def.def_id()`.

Resolves a definition id plus generic arguments into a concrete erased `Instance`, first erasing regions from the arguments and the combined query input and then invoking the compiler's instance-resolution query. It does not call other methods in the provided Methods List.

Resolves an instance suitable for conversion to a function pointer. It calls `Instance::try_resolve(...).ok().flatten()` and then rewrites the resolved definition when needed: it calls `resolved.def.requires_caller_location(tcx)` to turn tracked-caller items into `ReifyShim`, rewrites `Virtual` calls to `ReifyShim`, and under KCFI uses `tcx.opt_associated_item(def_id).and_then(...)`, `resolved.def_id()`, and `tcx.is_closure_like(...)` to decide when trait methods or closure-like calls must also be reified.

Resolves the callable instance to place in a vtable. It detects unsized-self trait methods and directly produces a `VTableShim`; otherwise it calls `Instance::resolve` and then post-processes the resolved instance, including calling `InstanceDef::requires_caller_location` to decide whether an `Item` must be converted into a caller-location-preserving shim or virtual form for trait-object dispatch.

Resolves a closure call instance by calling `args.as_closure().kind()` and `needs_fn_once_adapter_shim(actual_kind, requested_kind)`; if an adapter is needed it calls `Instance::fn_once_adapter_instance(...)`, otherwise it calls `Instance::new(def_id, args)`.

Resolves the `drop_in_place` lang-item instance for a concrete type by calling `tcx.require_lang_item(...)`, building arguments with `tcx.mk_args(...)`, and then calling `Instance::expect_resolve(...)` with `ty::TypingEnv::fully_monomorphized()` and a span derived from `ty.ty_adt_def().and_then(|adt| tcx.hir().span_if_local(adt.did())).unwrap_or(DUMMY_SP)`.

Builds the `ClosureOnceShim` instance used to adapt a closure to `FnOnce`. It calls `tcx.require_lang_item(...)`, `tcx.associated_items(...).in_definition_order().find(...).unwrap()` to locate `call_once`, checks `tcx.codegen_fn_attrs(closure_did).flags.contains(...)` for `track_caller`, constructs the closure self type with `Ty::new_closure(...)`, derives tupled inputs from `args.as_closure().sig().map_bound(...)`, erases bound regions with `tcx.instantiate_bound_regions_with_erased(...)`, and finishes by calling `tcx.mk_args_trait(...)`.

Returns a version of the instance whose generic arguments are reduced according to polymorphization analysis when the feature is enabled. It calls the free function `polymorphize` to compute the rewritten arguments and then rebuilds the instance with the same `def`.

Computes polymorphized generic arguments for an instance by removing or rewriting unused parameters, with special handling for closures and coroutines so captured nested callables are also normalized consistently. It calls `unused_generic_params` to get the unused-parameter mask, `def_id` to find the underlying definition, `type_of` and `skip_binder` to inspect the callable type, and then examines closure/coroutine argument structure via `kind`, `as_closure`, `tupled_upvars_ty`, `as_coroutine`, and `kind_ty`. When upvars are present, it uses the `PolymorphizationFolder` machinery, whose `fold_ty` recursively calls `polymorphize` on nested closure/coroutine types. It also uses helpers such as `is_some_and`, `tuple_fields`, `is_empty`, `fold_with`, `expect_ty`, `for_item`, `is_unused`, `unwrap`, `from`, and `mk_param_from_def` to rebuild the final argument list.

Determines whether adapting one closure kind to another requires a `FnOnce` adapter shim, returning `Ok(false)` when no shim is needed, `Ok(true)` for `Fn`/`FnMut` to `FnOnce`, and `Err(())` for unsupported conversions. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Converts an `InstanceDef` into its `WithOptConstParam<DefId>` form. For `Item`, it returns the stored definition directly; for shim, virtual, intrinsic, drop-glue, and clone-shim variants, it wraps the underlying `DefId` with `ty::WithOptConstParam::unknown`. Calls `ty::WithOptConstParam::unknown` for all non-`Item` variants.

Resolves an instance from a definition plus substitutions after erasing regions from the substitutions and query inputs. If the definition has an optional const argument, it calls `as_const_arg` and then `TyCtxt::resolve_instance_of_const_arg`; otherwise it calls `TyCtxt::resolve_instance`. Also calls `TyCtxt::erase_regions` on `substs`, `param_env.and(...)`, and the final query tuple inputs.
Returns `Some(self.substs)` when the instance definition has a polymorphic MIR body, otherwise `None`. Calls `has_polymorphic_mir_body` on `self.def`.

Applies the instance substitutions to a foldable MIR-related value only when the instance has a polymorphic MIR body; otherwise it returns the value unchanged. Calls `substs_for_mir_body`, and when substitutions are available, calls `EarlyBinder(...).subst`.

Substitutes MIR-body generics and normalizes while erasing regions. It calls `substs_for_mir_body`; if substitutions exist, it calls `TyCtxt::subst_and_normalize_erasing_regions`, otherwise it calls `TyCtxt::normalize_erasing_regions`.

Fallible version of MIR substitution plus normalization with region erasure. It calls `substs_for_mir_body`; if substitutions exist, it calls `TyCtxt::try_subst_and_normalize_erasing_regions`, otherwise it calls `TyCtxt::try_normalize_erasing_regions`.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the `PolymorphizationFolder`. It does not call any other listed methods.

Folds a type while polymorphizing closure and generator substitutions. It inspects the type kind, and for `Closure` and `Generator` cases it calls `polymorphize` using `ty::InstanceDef::Item(ty::WithOptConstParam::unknown(def_id))`; if substitutions changed, it rebuilds the type with `TyCtxt::mk_closure` or `TyCtxt::mk_generator`, otherwise it keeps the original type. For all other types, it calls `super_fold_with`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/shim.rs: Registers the shim query by assigning `make_shim` as the provider for `mir_shims`.

Main dispatcher that builds the appropriate MIR shim for an instance kind. It calls `build_call_shim` for vtable, function-pointer, reify, and closure-once call shims; calls `build_drop_shim` for non-generator drop glue; and calls `build_clone_shim` for clone shims. For generator drop glue, it reuses the optimized generator drop MIR directly instead of constructing a new drop shim.
Builds the MIR local declarations for a function signature by creating a return local from the output type and immutable argument locals from the input types.

Constructs MIR drop glue for a type or item by creating a minimal body, deriving locals with `local_decls_for_sig`, creating the body with `new_body`, and, when dropping a concrete type, elaborating the dereferenced drop through `elaborate_drops::elaborate_drop` before applying the resulting patch.
Creates a new MIR `Body` from the supplied source, blocks, locals, argument count, and span, initializing a single outermost source scope.
Implements `Debug` for `DropShimElaborator` as a no-op formatter that always returns success.
Returns the mutable `MirPatch` stored in the drop elaborator.
Returns the MIR body being elaborated.
Returns the type context associated with the drop elaborator.
Returns the parameter environment used for drop elaboration.
Selects drop elaboration style: `Static` for shallow drops of contained fields and `Open` for deep top-level drops that expand into a drop ladder.
Reports that this shim elaborator does not use drop flags by always returning `None`.
No-op hook for clearing drop flags, since drop shims do not track them.
Reports that field-specific subpaths are not modeled by returning `None`.
Reports that dereference-specific subpaths are not modeled by returning `None`.
Allows downcast traversal during elaboration by always returning `Some(())`.
Reports that array-element subpaths are not modeled by returning `None`.

Builds MIR for a clone shim. It creates a `CloneShimBuilder` with `CloneShimBuilder::new`, emits either `CloneShimBuilder::copy_shim` for `Copy` types or `CloneShimBuilder::tuple_like_shim` for closures and tuples, and finally returns the body with `CloneShimBuilder::into_mir`.
Initializes a clone-shim builder by substituting the concrete self type into the signature and creating local declarations with `local_decls_for_sig`.
Finishes the clone-shim builder by packaging its accumulated blocks and locals into a MIR body with `new_body`.
Builds outermost `SourceInfo` for the builder's span.
Appends a basic block with the builder's current `source_info`. It calls `source_info` to populate the block terminator metadata.
Computes a future basic-block index by adding an offset to the current block count.
Creates a MIR statement tagged with the builder's current `source_info`. It calls `source_info` to fill the statement metadata.

Emits the simple clone shim for `Copy` types by assigning the dereferenced receiver into the return place. It calls `make_statement` to build the assignment statement and `block` to emit the returning block.
Allocates a new local of the requested type and mutability and returns it as a MIR place.

Emits one MIR call to `Clone::clone` for a field or element. It calls `make_place` to allocate temporary reference storage, `make_statement` to create the borrow assignment, and `block` to emit the call terminator with normal and cleanup successors.

Builds clone MIR for tuple-like aggregates by cloning each field in order and adding cleanup blocks that drop already-cloned fields on unwind. It calls `block_index_offset` to compute successor blocks, `make_clone_call` for each field clone, and `block` to emit cleanup and final return blocks.

Constructs MIR for call-forwarding shims, adjusting the receiver as needed and forwarding arguments to either a direct callee or an indirect function pointer. It uses `local_decls_for_sig` to derive locals for the synthesized signature.

Builds MIR for an ADT constructor by normalizing the constructor signature, generating aggregate-assignment statements into the return place, creating locals with `local_decls_for_sig`, and packaging the result with `new_body`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/abi.rs::l: Resolves an ABI name string to its corresponding `Abi` by iterating over `AbiDatas`, finding the entry whose `name` matches the input, and mapping that entry to its `abi` variant. It does not call any other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/abi.rs::a: Returns a vector containing every known ABI name by iterating over `AbiDatas`, extracting each entry’s `name`, and collecting the results. It does not call any other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/abi.rs::i: Computes the stable numeric index for an `Abi` variant with a fixed match table that must remain synchronized with `AbiDatas`; it also performs a debug-only verification that the computed index matches the variant’s position in `AbiDatas`. It does not call any other methods from the provided Methods List.
Returns the canonical `AbiData` entry for this `Abi` by indexing into `AbiDatas`. This method calls `impl Abi::index` to obtain the array position.
Returns the canonical string name of this `Abi` by reading the `name` field from its associated `AbiData`. This method calls `impl Abi::data`.
Formats an `Abi` for display as its quoted ABI name. This method calls `impl Abi::name` to obtain the textual name before writing it to the formatter.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Traverses all item-like nodes in the given module and runs `CollectItemTypesVisitor` over them to trigger collection/type-signature queries. It calls `tcx.hir()` and then `deep_visit_item_likes_in_module`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pr: Registers this module’s collection-related query providers, wiring functions such as `collect_mod_item_types`, `generics_of`, `predicates_of`, `fn_sig`, `trait_def`, `adt_def`, `impl_trait_ref`, `impl_polarity`, `generator_kind`, `codegen_fn_attrs`, and others into `Providers`. It does not meaningfully call other methods from the list; it assigns them as query hooks.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Visits a HIR type, records the span when the type is an inferred placeholder `_`, and then continues recursive traversal. It calls `intravisit::walk_ty`.
Visits a generic argument, records placeholder inference arguments, recursively walks inferred args, and forwards type arguments to the type visitor. It calls `intravisit::walk_inf` and `visit_ty`.
Visits an array length, records the span for inferred array lengths, and then continues recursive traversal. It calls `intravisit::walk_array_len`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pl: Emits an error for illegal placeholder types in item signatures when any placeholder spans were collected. It returns early for an empty list; otherwise it calls `placeholder_type_error_diag` and then emits the resulting diagnostic with `emit`.

Builds the detailed diagnostic for illegal placeholder types in item signatures, including generic-parameter-based suggestions and special handling for bare function types in const/static contexts. If no placeholder spans are present it calls `bad_placeholder`; otherwise it also calls `bad_placeholder` to create the base diagnostic, then inspects HIR parents via `tcx.hir()` to decide whether to attach suggestions.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ba: Creates the base E0121 diagnostic for placeholder `_` appearing in item-signature types, pluralizes the item kind, sorts spans, and labels each offending span. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ad: Constructs the `ty::AdtDef` for a local enum, struct, or union by converting each HIR variant into compiler metadata. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::tr: Builds the compiler's `ty::TraitDef` for a local trait or trait alias, collecting flags such as auto-trait status, unsafety, marker/specialization attributes, and validating trait-level attributes like `rustc_paren_sugar` and `rustc_must_implement_one_of`. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ha: Helper for late-bound-region detection on a specific function signature. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Visits generic parameters to detect whether the target anonymous const appears inside a const parameter's type. For const params, it temporarily marks `in_param_ty` and calls `visit_ty` on the parameter type.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Computes the `ty::Generics` for a local definition by determining its generic parent, handling special cases such as impl/trait items, variant ctors, fields, anonymous consts, opaque types, and closures, and extracting the in-scope parameters. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Extracts a function return type only when it is an inferable/suggestable placeholder. It calls `is_suggestable_infer_ty` on `FnRetTy::Return` and returns that type if suggestion logic should handle it.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::in: Computes a function signature while special-casing placeholder return types to reuse typeck inference and emit a tailored diagnostic. It calls `get_infer_ret_ty` to detect inferable returns; when present, it uses `typeck(...).liberated_fn_sigs()` to obtain the inferred signature, visits the placeholder type with `HirPlaceholderCollector::visit_ty`, builds a diagnostic with `bad_placeholder`, may call `fn_sig` on a returned function definition for better suggestions, and otherwise falls back to `AstConv::ty_of_fn`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Computes the implemented trait reference for an impl item, if any. It calls `type_of` to obtain the impl self type and `AstConv::instantiate_mono_trait_ref` to lower the HIR trait path into a monomorphic `ty::TraitRef`.

Determines whether an impl is positive, negative, or reservation, and emits errors for invalid uses of `#[rustc_reservation_impl]`. It inspects the impl HIR and attribute state, using `span_err` for disallowed negative or inherent reservation impls.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ea: Iterates the lifetime parameters from a `hir::Generics` that are early-bound rather than late-bound. It filters `generics.params` by calling `is_late_bound` and keeping only lifetime params for which that returns `false`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pr: Builds the predicates defined directly on `def_id` by starting from `explicit_predicates_of` and, when present, appending `inferred_outlives_of` predicates to the result.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ga: Collects the explicit predicates written for a local item by inspecting its HIR node, generics, and item kind, setting up trait/default-impl context as needed, and assembling the resulting `GenericPredicates` from the item’s declared bounds and related inherited information.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Traverses a local item to gather `ConstEvaluatable` predicates from anonymous consts. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Handles an anonymous const during traversal by converting it to a const value and, if it is unevaluated, inserting a `ConstEvaluatable` predicate for it into the collector.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pr: Converts a single HIR generic bound into predicates by calling `add_bounds` on the `AstConv` and then extracting the resulting predicates from the accumulated bounds.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Computes the polymorphic signature of a foreign function declaration by calling `AstConv::ty_of_fn`, choosing intrinsic unsafety when needed via `intrinsic_operation_unsafety`, and then checking the resulting input/output types for gated SIMD FFI usage.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::is: Returns whether a local `def_id` corresponds to a HIR `ForeignItem`, and bugs out if the `DefId` is non-local.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Returns the generator kind for a local closure expression by looking up the closure body and querying its `generator_kind`; returns `None` for non-closure locals and bugs on non-local `DefId`s.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::fr: Parses a `#[target_feature]` attribute, validates each requested feature against the target and enabled feature gates, emits diagnostics for malformed or unsupported entries, and appends accepted features to `target_features`.
